\[
I_{\text{out}} = m + \frac{\max\bigl(0,\, s^2 - n^2\bigr)}{\max\bigl(s^2,\, n^2\bigr)}\,(z - m)
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(m\): The local mean
- \(s^2\): The local variance
- \(n\): The noise standard deviation
- \(z\): The pixel value

m and s squared are the mean and variance of the window, z is the pixel and n is the noise sigma. Where the window varies about as much as the noise, the gain is near 0 and the output is the local mean. Where it varies much more, there is real detail, the gain is near 1 and the pixel is kept. This is the estimate of Lee (1980) for additive noise, in the form of MATLAB's wiener2 and scipy.signal.wiener. Those estimate n squared from the whole image when it is not given. Here it is a parameter, so a strip of the image gives the same result as the whole image.
